svg.aria-label: How to write ç: 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 2 movements
svg.title: Writing ç
svg.desc: 2 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ç (latin), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/LatinPrint-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after By analogy with the cited é and ñ, not separately sourced: the c after the Grundschrift-App, level kleinbuchstaben/c (assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/c/metadata.json, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only), then the cedilla last, as UJIpenchars2's native Spanish writers draw the marks of é and ñ (UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) <https://github.com/Medien-Treibhaus/grundschrift-app-source/blob/f6dbd807adbb3fc2f94207fe578def439f6e9c49/assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/c/metadata.json>. Source note on variation: ORDER BY ANALOGY, NOT SEPARATELY SOURCED. No source reachable here records how ç is written: the Grundschrift-App has no letter with this mark, and UJIpenchars2 holds Spanish characters only. So its order is drawn by analogy with the cited é and ñ. UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) finds the accent of é drawn last, after the e, in all 120 of its traces, and the tilde of ñ last, after the n, in all 108 where it is a separate mark (104 of them from left to right). ç is therefore the Grundschrift-App's c (level kleinbuchstaben/c, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only), then the cedilla after it. No source reachable here records the direction of this mark, so it is drawn left to right and top to bottom, the direction these records give every mark no cited record covers. The cedilla hangs from the foot of the c, so it runs down from there and round to the left, along the printed hook. Only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are claimed, and only by analogy; no point is copied, and the path is fitted to the ç of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer.
